subject: Reseller Addendum: escrow chain & signer authority validation
messages:
From: Acme Cloud Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodai.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodai.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Reseller addendum — confirmation of escrow & signer path

Hi Lauren / Ben,

Thanks for taking the time on the call yesterday. Our procurement/legal team reviewed the reseller addendum and has two open items before we can sign the order form:

1) Escrow / invoice pass-through: we need explicit language showing the escrow sequence (seller -> marketplace -> reseller) and an attestation window for invoice evidence (90 days). Can Redwood confirm the operations flow and who owns the invoice metadata in a pass-through case?

2) Signer authority: for our regional resellers we require either a signatory matrix or a POA on file. The current addendum refers generically to "authorized signers" — please provide the signer validation approach (how you and the reseller will handle NDA/POA).

Attached our procurement checklist for reference. Can we get proposed redlines by EOD Thursday? We’re targeting a June 1 go-live.

Thanks,

Mark Jones
Acme Cloud — Senior Counsel (contracts)
procurement@acmecloud.com

Attachment: acme_procurement_checklist_v3.pdf

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodai.com>
To: Acme Cloud Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodai.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 13:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Reseller addendum — confirmation of escrow & signer path

Mark — thanks for the clear notes and the checklist. High-level responses and next steps below.

Escrow / invoice pass-through: Redwood recognizes the need for explicit sequencing. Operationally we propose the invoice metadata remain with the original seller (Acme) and a pass-through ledger entry on our side. That gives you an auditable trace while letting Redwood act as the conduit. We will propose a clause that: (a) enumerates the ledger fields (invoice_id, invoice_date, amount, reseller_id), (b) requires retention for 90 days after payment, and (c) permits a limited audit right.

Signer authority: we can support a signer matrix in Appendix A. For edge cases where the reseller is a middle-man with delegated signing, Redwood will accept a notarized POA or a company attestation signed by two officers.

I’m including Karthik for legal redlines and Ben for billing/ops details. I’ve attached our initial redline with placeholders for the ledger fields and an example signer matrix.

Proposed timeline: Karthik to send legal redlines by Wed EOD (our side); we’ll consolidate and return to you by Thu COB. Does that work for your 6/1 target?

Cheers,

Lauren Bishop
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodai.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redline-reseller-addendum_Lauren_v1.pdf

Subject: Re: Reseller addendum — confirmation of escrow & signer path

Lauren / Ben / Mark — I reviewed Lauren's draft and have a few substantive changes and one ask for ops to confirm. Summary below and attached detailed comments.

1) Escrow language: replace the proposed "limited audit right" with a clearer audit trigger (material discrepancy or invoice dispute only). We must avoid an open-ended audit right that could be abused. Suggest: "Redwood will provide audit evidence within 10 business days following receipt of a written dispute that includes invoice identifiers."

2) Data retention: 90 days is acceptable for ledger visibility, but we need to be explicit that customer PII will be redacted from any evidentiary export unless there is a lawful request. Add a short carriage return to the retention clause to reflect that.

3) Signer matrix: fine to include Appendix A, but we should add acceptance criteria: (a) POA must be notarized; (b) attestation must include signatory name, title, and corporate registry ID; (c) Redwood reserves the right to request additional proof in the event of suspected fraud.

Ops question for Ben: when we pass ledger fields through the platform, can we programmatically tag invoice_id and generate an audit bundle within 48 hours of a dispute? If not, we need to extend the response window in the clause.

I attached my redline (tracked changes) and a short snippet we can use for Appendix A. If ops confirms 48-hour bundle creation, legal is fine with the 10 business day response window.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodai.com

Attachment: legal-comments_karthik.docx

From: Mark Jones <m.jones@joneslegal.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodai.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodai.com>
Date: Thu, 16 May 2028 18:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Reseller addendum — confirmation of escrow & signer path

Karthik / Lauren — appreciate the quick turnaround and the drafting approach. A couple of notes from Acme Legal: 

• The audit trigger language you propose is reasonable, but we need to retain an option for an independent auditor in the case of billing disputes exceeding $250k. Can Redwood accept an independent auditor clause limited to such thresholds?

• POA: notarized POA is acceptable but our reseller network often relies on regional partners that do not have a formal notarization process. As a practical alternative we can provide a certified corporate registry extract plus a sworn attestation from the reseller CEO — would Redwood accept that as an alternative to notarization?

Action items:
1) Can Redwood confirm whether the ops team can produce an audit bundle within 48 hours of a dispute? Ben — can you confirm and, if not, propose the operational SLA you can commit to?
2) Karthik — if Redwood accepts the certified-extract + sworn-attestation alternative, can you add that language to Appendix A?

If we can align on those two items by tomorrow, we’ll circulate the final order form for signature and route it through our procurement queue.

Thanks,

Mark Jones
Senior Counsel
Acme Cloud
procurement@acmecloud.com
